item.text: {"0":"Across all four datasets, jointly reduce Adam learning rate from 1e-3 to 7e-4 and increase dropout from 0.1 to 0.15. Slower updates coupled with stronger regularization may improve generalization of the normalized embeddings and recurrent states. Preserve all other settings, including embedding parameterization, GRU topology, causal readout, loss, history policy, seed 42, 200-epoch cap and 200 batches per epoch. Train one model per category.","1":"Across all four datasets, soften item embedding normalization from e/||e|| to e/max(||e||,1e-12)^0.9 for both history and candidate lookups, keeping padding exactly zero. This permits modest learned norm variation while retaining most directional normalization, potentially recovering item-specific confidence. Keep dimensions, GRU topology, features, readout, scoring formula, loss and optimizer fixed. Synchronize the predictor writer and checkpoint metadata; retain one model per category.","2":"Across all four datasets, derive adjacent-item transition counts solely from training histories. For each observed history item with a real predecessor, multiply its input embedding by 1+0.05*c/(c+5), where c is that ordered pair's training count; use scale 1 otherwise. Recurrent inputs may benefit from distinguishing supported transitions. This fixed input feature adds no prediction score or learned module. Preserve embedding design, GRU topology, readout, loss and optimizer; checkpoint the count table and reproduce preprocessing in the predictor writer.","3":"Across all four datasets, replace only the pairwise term softplus(s_neg-s_pos) with 1.5*softplus((s_neg-s_pos)/1.5), retaining the pointwise coefficient 0.2 and valid-position averaging. The broader logistic transition may maintain useful gradients for already separated pairs without introducing the positive margin that regressed. Preserve features, embeddings, GRU topology, readout, scoring, optimizer, sampling, scheduler and batch/epoch settings. Retain one model per category."}
